title: Microsoft 365 Copilot: admins manage federated Copilot connectors in the Microsoft 365 admin center
summary: The briefing passes: its roadmap facts, licensing, admin paths and preview Graph automation are supported by the sources checked. It distinguishes the administration change's unstated arrival default from connector availability and accurately reports Microsoft's differing role guidance.

claims.claim: Admins can govern and manage federated Copilot connectors in the Microsoft 365 admin center.
claims.quote: Admins can govern and manage federated copilot connectors in Microsoft 365 admin center. #copilotcontrolsystem

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Governance guidance; controls[0]
claims.claim: Agent and plugin access allows or blocks federated connectors by Microsoft, organization or external publisher type.
claims.quote: Turn off all connectors of a publisher type (Microsoft, your organization, or external publishers) in a single step.

claims.claim: The publisher-type choice also applies to future connectors of that type.
claims.quote: Apply that choice automatically to future connectors of that type.

claims.claim: User access is the tenant-wide maximum population for agents and plugins, including federated connectors.
claims.quote: User access doesn't turn connectors on or off; it sets the maximum population. A connector whose details pane shows Everyone is still unavailable to users excluded by User access.

claims.claim: Admins can enable or disable an individual connector.
claims.quote: Enable or disable connectors at the tenant level.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance: At rollout; controls[2].note
claims.claim: Add staging in the Staged rollout column limits a connector to users or Microsoft Entra ID groups.
claims.quote: Limit a connector to specific users or Microsoft Entra ID groups by choosing Add staging in the Staged rollout column. Staging can't extend beyond the users allowed by User access.

claims.claim: An individual connector setting takes precedence over the bulk Agent and plugin access setting.
claims.quote: A setting you make on an individual connector takes precedence over the bulk Agent and plugin access setting.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: User access always applies and connector staging cannot widen its population.
claims.quote: Only these users can use any connector. Connector staging can narrow but not widen this population.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Changes can take up to 10 minutes to take effect.
claims.quote: Changes can take up to 10 minutes to take effect across Microsoft 365 experiences.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Where a connector provides the tools, Copilot can create, update or delete data in the connected system on the user's behalf.
claims.quote: Where a connector provides the tools, Copilot can also create, update, or delete data in the connected system on the user's behalf.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Governance guidance; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Write, update and delete tools initially require the user's explicit approval.
claims.quote: Tools that create, update, or delete data initially require the user's explicit approval. Users can choose whether Copilot asks again for that tool, as described in Confirm an action.

claims.claim: Federated connectors remain read-only in the Researcher agent.
claims.quote: The Researcher agent doesn't support write, update, or delete actions. Federated Copilot connectors remain read-only in this experience.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: Write, update and delete tools are part of the connector and are not enabled separately.

claims.quote: View a connector's tools in the admin center (Coming soon)

claims.quote: Microsoft-built federated connectors are available by default when you select Allow agents and plugins built by Microsoft in Agent and plugin access and include the user in User access.

claims.where: Why it matters; Governance guidance: Before rollout; controls[1].note
claims.claim: User access defaults to All users.
claims.quote: All users - This option is the default. It means that all users in the organization can access agents and plugins, subject to the existing app policies and user assignments.

claims.claim: External-publisher connectors are available only when that publisher option is selected or an admin enables the connector individually.
claims.quote: Connectors from external publishers are available only when you select Allow agents and plugins built by external publishers, or when an admin turns on the individual connector.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; Why it matters
claims.claim: Microsoft has not stated the arrival default for this administration change, so defaultState is unknown.
claims.quote: Searched: 'federated connectors admin governance management default rollout admin controls enabled default'. Read roadmap, manage, overview and agent-settings pages; they give connector/User access defaults, not whether this administration change starts enforcing on arrival.

claims.claim: Microsoft warns that data processed by non-Microsoft services is not subject to Microsoft agreements.
claims.quote: Data processed by non-Microsoft services isn't subject to Microsoft agreements. Review the terms provided by non-Microsoft agent and plugin publishers

claims.quote: Users authenticate by using their own credentials when prompted to connect to the data sources.

claims.claim: The source system enforces the user's permissions for both reading and modifying data.

claims.claim: For an MCP server restricting incoming traffic by source IP, Microsoft instructs admins to allow Copilot's static egress IP addresses.
claims.quote: If your MCP server restricts incoming traffic by source IP address, configure its firewall to allow the static egress IP addresses used by Microsoft 365 Copilot.

claims.claim: Static egress is enabled by default for MCP-based federated connectors.
claims.quote: Static egress is enabled by default for MCP-based federated connectors.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Users can choose Allow for conversation for an individual tool.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Users can choose Always allow for an individual tool.
claims.quote: Always allow | Runs the action and doesn't ask again for this tool until the user changes the setting or the publisher changes the tool.

claims.quote: If the option stays selected, new connectors of that type follow the default rollout and are available to everyone included in User access.
